sources.title: Suspected North Korean hackers steal $5.6 billion in crypto in record-breaking cryptocurrency heist, Binance withdrawals frozen — firm says it will cover losses as stablecoin networks move to freeze $2.4b in stolen assets - Tom's Hardware
passages: From hereon, this month shall be called SpookITober.

In yet another high-profile cybersecurity incident this month, Binance.com, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been hacked , to the tune of $5.6 billion taken in various cryptocurrencies.

As of this writing, withdrawals at the exchange are suspended until the company sorts out the situation, though it has stated repeatedly that "user funds remain safe," adding that it "will cover all losses." The U.S.-specific Binance.us website is so far reportedly unaffected.
At least two security agencies, including TRM , have pinned the attack on an elite North Korean hacking unit.
For what it's worth, the company has a means of insurance and a reasonable track record in these situations, though the amount of bullion pilfered today is exorbitant.
"TRM attributes this attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s premier hacking unit," the security firm said.
Per TRM, this latest instance bears many of the same hallmarks as earlier North Korean heists.

According to CNN , an unnamed analyst at Pangolin Intelligence corroborated this story by "Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]."
Back in May 2019, thieves made out with 7,000 BTC from Binance, amounting to around $40 million at the time.
The company covered the entirety of the losses with SAFU funds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware.

Preliminary info breaks down the stolen amounts like so: $1.57b in Tether dollars (USDT), $1.45b in Bitcoin (BTC), $875m in Ethereum (ETH), $823m in Circle dollars (USDC), $234m in Tron (TRX), $88.5m in Ripple dollars (RLUSD), $75M in Wrapped-Beacon Ethereum (WBETH), $50m in Tether Gold (XAUT), and $447.5 million in other cryptocurrencies.
Note that this is a developing story, so the tallies are subject to change.
Should that amount be final, this heist would exceed the $1.5b stolen from Bybit in February 2025, of which only a paltry portion has so far been recovered.
There's little info so far on the miscreant's means of larceny.
Apparently, the Binance 14 , Binance 16 , and Hot Wallet 34 hot wallets, which hold pooled customer funds, were drained.
It's currently not known if this happened via stolen private keys, a compromised signing process, or another type of intrusion.

Update, Friday 30 Oct, 6:30 am ET: This developing story has been updated with information from Binance regarding how its system was compromised, and reports from security outlets claiming North Korea may be responsible.
These details have been added to the story below.

The stablecoin issuers all moved to blacklist the thief's main wallet (you can see it here on the Ethereum blockchain) in their smart contracts, a move that means the amounts in USDT, USDC, and RLUSD are frozen in place, totaling around $2.4 billion.

sources.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history - BBC
passages: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."

Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind. Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector. The incident, disclosed on Thursday evening, represents the largest reported cryptocurrency theft on record, according to the exchange. Binance said it had worked with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion in affected assets and would cover all losses using its own funds. The exchange expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours, subject to the completion of additional security checks. Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines. Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed that an attacker had exploited a security vulnerability to carry out unauthorised withdrawals. The company estimated the total financial impact at $6.3 billion, making the incident substantially larger than previous cryptocurrency exchange hacks. According to Binance, the breach originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer. The attacker used the compromised device to execute unauthorised withdrawals from the exchange. Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed. The distinction is significant because private keys provide direct control over digital assets held in cryptocurrency wallets. The company has temporarily halted withdrawals while it conducts security checks and works to prevent further unauthorised transactions. Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures. Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack. The exchange also committed to reimbursing all losses from its own financial resources. Circle, the company behind the USDC stablecoin, confirmed that it had frozen more than 800 million USDC linked to the breach. Tether separately reported freezing more than 1.567 billion USDT associated with the attack. The measures were intended to prevent the movement of stolen funds and limit the financial consequences of the incident. Binance co-founder and former Chief Executive Changpeng Zhao also commented on the situation. "It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post. The company's commitment to cover losses and restore withdrawals will remain an important factor in determining how quickly confidence returns among its users. According to its data, the stolen assets included approximately $1.66 billion in Tether's USDT stablecoin. The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time. A further $767 million in USDC was transferred from the exchange. The figures illustrate the scale and diversity of the digital assets involved in the incident. Glassnode also reported that Binance's holdings of its native BNB token were "left untouched." The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies. Cryptocurrency prices declined following the disclosure of the security breach, extending losses recorded earlier in the week. Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60. During the initial market reaction, the token dropped as low as $76,518 before recovering part of its losses. The selloff reflected concerns about exchange security, the potential impact on market liquidity and uncertainty surrounding the recovery of stolen assets. The temporary suspension of withdrawals also added to investor caution as Binance worked to complete its security review. The market reaction extended beyond cryptocurrencies to publicly traded companies with significant exposure to digital assets. The latest security incident introduced additional uncertainty for businesses whose performance is closely linked to the adoption and trading of digital assets. The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services. The exchange has indicated that withdrawals should resume within 48 hours and that it intends to absorb the financial losses associated with the incident.

sources.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto
passages: Crypto watchers say at least $2 billion has been drained from Binance’s hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets that store crypto that are connected to the internet.
By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing.
Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary said that Binance has “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.”
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.
If confirmed into the billions, this would likely rank as one of the largest crypto breaches in history, according to leaderboards tracking crypto thefts.

In yet another high-profile cybersecurity incident this month, Binance.com, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been hacked , to the tune of $5.6 billion taken in various cryptocurrencies.

As of this writing, withdrawals at the exchange are suspended until the company sorts out the situation, though it has stated repeatedly that "user funds remain safe," adding that it "will cover all losses." The U.S.-specific Binance.us website is so far reportedly unaffected.
At least two security agencies, including TRM , have pinned the attack on an elite North Korean hacking unit.
For what it's worth, the company has a means of insurance and a reasonable track record in these situations, though the amount of bullion pilfered today is exorbitant.
"TRM attributes this attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s premier hacking unit," the security firm said.
Per TRM, this latest instance bears many of the same hallmarks as earlier North Korean heists.

According to CNN , an unnamed analyst at Pangolin Intelligence corroborated this story by "Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]."
Back in May 2019, thieves made out with 7,000 BTC from Binance, amounting to around $40 million at the time.
The company covered the entirety of the losses with SAFU funds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware.

Preliminary info breaks down the stolen amounts like so: $1.57b in Tether dollars (USDT), $1.45b in Bitcoin (BTC), $875m in Ethereum (ETH), $823m in Circle dollars (USDC), $234m in Tron (TRX), $88.5m in Ripple dollars (RLUSD), $75M in Wrapped-Beacon Ethereum (WBETH), $50m in Tether Gold (XAUT), and $447.5 million in other cryptocurrencies.
Note that this is a developing story, so the tallies are subject to change.
Should that amount be final, this heist would exceed the $1.5b stolen from Bybit in February 2025, of which only a paltry portion has so far been recovered.
There's little info so far on the miscreant's means of larceny.
Apparently, the Binance 14 , Binance 16 , and Hot Wallet 34 hot wallets, which hold pooled customer funds, were drained.
It's currently not known if this happened via stolen private keys, a compromised signing process, or another type of intrusion.

These details have been added to the story below.

The stablecoin issuers all moved to blacklist the thief's main wallet (you can see it here on the Ethereum blockchain) in their smart contracts, a move that means the amounts in USDT, USDC, and RLUSD are frozen in place, totaling around $2.4 billion.

story.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto

facts.text: From hereon, this month shall be called SpookITober.

In yet another high-profile cybersecurity incident this month, Binance.com, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been hacked , to the tune of $5.6 billion taken in various cryptocurrencies.

As of this writing, withdrawals at the exchange are suspended until the company sorts out the situation, though it has stated repeatedly that "user funds remain safe," adding that it "will cover all losses." The U.S.-specific Binance.us website is so far reportedly unaffected.
At least two security agencies, including TRM , have pinned the attack on an elite North Korean hacking unit.
For what it's worth, the company has a means of insurance and a reasonable track record in these situations, though the amount of bullion pilfered today is exorbitant.
"TRM attributes this attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s premier hacking unit," the security firm said.
Per TRM, this latest instance bears many of the same hallmarks as earlier North Korean heists.

According to CNN , an unnamed analyst at Pangolin Intelligence corroborated this story by "Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]."
Back in May 2019, thieves made out with 7,000 BTC from Binance, amounting to around $40 million at the time.
The company covered the entirety of the losses with SAFU funds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware.

Preliminary info breaks down the stolen amounts like so: $1.57b in Tether dollars (USDT), $1.45b in Bitcoin (BTC), $875m in Ethereum (ETH), $823m in Circle dollars (USDC), $234m in Tron (TRX), $88.5m in Ripple dollars (RLUSD), $75M in Wrapped-Beacon Ethereum (WBETH), $50m in Tether Gold (XAUT), and $447.5 million in other cryptocurrencies.
Note that this is a developing story, so the tallies are subject to change.
Should that amount be final, this heist would exceed the $1.5b stolen from Bybit in February 2025, of which only a paltry portion has so far been recovered.
There's little info so far on the miscreant's means of larceny.
Apparently, the Binance 14 , Binance 16 , and Hot Wallet 34 hot wallets, which hold pooled customer funds, were drained.
It's currently not known if this happened via stolen private keys, a compromised signing process, or another type of intrusion.

Update, Friday 30 Oct, 6:30 am ET: This developing story has been updated with information from Binance regarding how its system was compromised, and reports from security outlets claiming North Korea may be responsible.
These details have been added to the story below.

The stablecoin issuers all moved to blacklist the thief's main wallet (you can see it here on the Ethereum blockchain) in their smart contracts, a move that means the amounts in USDT, USDC, and RLUSD are frozen in place, totaling around $2.4 billion.

Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines.
The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time.
Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60.
Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack.
The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.
The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services.
Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post.
Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed.
Crypto watchers say at least $2 billion has been drained from Binance’s hot wallets, which are internet-connected cryptocurrency wallets that store crypto that are connected to the internet.
By some estimates, Binance may have lost upward of $5.7 billion in crypto , though the numbers have not been confirmed and it’s possible that the theft is ongoing.
Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary said that Binance has “temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure.”
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” Binance said in a statement.

“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Zhao, who no longer runs the company but is its largest shareholder, said that he expects users’ funds to be “fully covered” but did not provide an explanation for the claim.
If confirmed into the billions, this would likely rank as one of the largest crypto breaches in history, according to leaderboards tracking crypto thefts.

sources.title: Suspected North Korean hackers steal $5.6 billion in crypto in record-breaking cryptocurrency heist, Binance withdrawals frozen — firm says it will cover losses as stablecoin networks move to freeze $2.4b in stolen assets - Tom's Hardware
passages: From hereon, this month shall be called SpookITober.

In yet another high-profile cybersecurity incident this month, Binance.com, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has been hacked , to the tune of $5.6 billion taken in various cryptocurrencies.

As of this writing, withdrawals at the exchange are suspended until the company sorts out the situation, though it has stated repeatedly that "user funds remain safe," adding that it "will cover all losses." The U.S.-specific Binance.us website is so far reportedly unaffected.
At least two security agencies, including TRM , have pinned the attack on an elite North Korean hacking unit.
For what it's worth, the company has a means of insurance and a reasonable track record in these situations, though the amount of bullion pilfered today is exorbitant.
"TRM attributes this attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s premier hacking unit," the security firm said.
Per TRM, this latest instance bears many of the same hallmarks as earlier North Korean heists.

According to CNN , an unnamed analyst at Pangolin Intelligence corroborated this story by "Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents [involving the North Korean cyber unit]."
Back in May 2019, thieves made out with 7,000 BTC from Binance, amounting to around $40 million at the time.
The company covered the entirety of the losses with SAFU funds.
Bruno Ferreira is a contributing writer for Tom's Hardware.

Preliminary info breaks down the stolen amounts like so: $1.57b in Tether dollars (USDT), $1.45b in Bitcoin (BTC), $875m in Ethereum (ETH), $823m in Circle dollars (USDC), $234m in Tron (TRX), $88.5m in Ripple dollars (RLUSD), $75M in Wrapped-Beacon Ethereum (WBETH), $50m in Tether Gold (XAUT), and $447.5 million in other cryptocurrencies.
Note that this is a developing story, so the tallies are subject to change.
Should that amount be final, this heist would exceed the $1.5b stolen from Bybit in February 2025, of which only a paltry portion has so far been recovered.
There's little info so far on the miscreant's means of larceny.
Apparently, the Binance 14 , Binance 16 , and Hot Wallet 34 hot wallets, which hold pooled customer funds, were drained.
It's currently not known if this happened via stolen private keys, a compromised signing process, or another type of intrusion.

Update, Friday 30 Oct, 6:30 am ET: This developing story has been updated with information from Binance regarding how its system was compromised, and reports from security outlets claiming North Korea may be responsible.
These details have been added to the story below.

The stablecoin issuers all moved to blacklist the thief's main wallet (you can see it here on the Ethereum blockchain) in their smart contracts, a move that means the amounts in USDT, USDC, and RLUSD are frozen in place, totaling around $2.4 billion.

sources.title: Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history - BBC
passages: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".

extraction.body: Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record. The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses". The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach". Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor. Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack. Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record". AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen. The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody. The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack. For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens. The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past. Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets. Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice." The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue. Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop. "That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement. In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them." Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them." In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets. "Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said. Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack. World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds. Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation. Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue. Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply. The cyber-attack, which the company describes as complex, is believed to be the largest ever of its kind. Cyber correspondent Joe Tidy explains more about what is suspected to be the biggest hack in history. sources.title: Binance Suspends Withdrawals After $6.3 Billion Cryptocurrency Hack as Bitcoin and Crypto Stocks Fall - Yahoo Finance
passages: Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals after reporting a security breach involving approximately $6.3 billion in stolen digital assets, triggering losses across cryptocurrency markets and shares of companies exposed to the sector.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Bitcoin fell sharply following the announcement, while Ether, Binance's BNB token and several cryptocurrency-related stocks also recorded significant declines.
The attacker also withdrew 17,985 Bitcoin, valued at approximately $1.45 billion at the time.
Bitcoin, the world's largest cryptocurrency by market capitalisation, fell 2.5% to $78,106.60.
Binance said it had coordinated with industry partners to freeze approximately $3 billion of the assets affected by the attack.
The absence of a reported reduction in BNB holdings contrasted with the substantial losses involving Bitcoin, stablecoins and other cryptocurrencies.
The immediate focus for cryptocurrency markets will be Binance's progress in completing its security checks and restoring withdrawal services.
Binance indicated that it expects the suspension to last no longer than 48 hours, although the resumption of withdrawals remains dependent on the completion of its security procedures.
"It does look like a hack on Binance," Zhao said in a social media post.
Binance said its investigation had found no evidence that private keys associated with cryptocurrency wallets had been exposed.

Researchers describe the network of hackers, known in the cybersecurity industry as TraderTraitor, as a North Korean cell focused almost exclusively on stealing crypto from large companies and exchanges.
Blockchain security firm Elliptic also attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers.

Companies regularly ask third-party companies to stress-test their security to identify weaknesses that could be exploited by attackers, but it’s unclear if Binance sought such a review.

That figure surpasses the 2025 Bybit theft, previously regarded as the largest known cryptocurrency heist on record. Binance estimated its own impact at approximately $6.3 billion and temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks, according to the company's official statement on X. Binance's preliminary investigation identified a potentially compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, though the company later noted additional points of breach. Binance's preliminary investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop as a likely entry point. Attackers may have used that access to reach a service container, then submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions from there. Binance said it found no evidence that private keys were leaked. Private keys are the cryptographic credentials that directly authorize control over cryptocurrency holdings, so their absence suggests attackers exploited an operational pathway rather than the most direct form of account control. The alleged method raises questions about whether privileged employee devices and associated environments had excessive access to systems capable of authorizing withdrawals at this scale. TRM Labs, Elliptic, and Chainalysis each attributed the attack to North Korea, though those assessments rest on blockchain tracing and pattern analysis rather than a completed criminal indictment. TRM Labs attributed the attack to TraderTraitor , describing it as an elite North Korean hacking unit. The firm said it reached that assessment with high confidence, according to Reuters. Elliptic cited similarities between this fund movement and patterns seen in earlier attacks linked to the same network, according to the Wall Street Journal. Chainalysis also assessed the breach as likely conducted by TraderTraitor, according to CBS News. Those assessments rest on blockchain tracing, infrastructure analysis, and attack-pattern comparison. No public criminal indictment has been filed in connection with this specific incident, and North Korean responsibility should be read as a converging set of private-sector assessments rather than a settled legal finding. The alleged financial motive is consistent with longstanding assessments by U.S. government and international bodies that North Korean cyber operations generate hard currency for a heavily sanctioned state, including programs tied to weapons development. Roughly $3 billion of the affected assets have been frozen on-chain, while the remainder is still being traced across multiple blockchains. Roughly $3 billion of the affected assets have been frozen on-chain through cooperation with blockchain partners, according to Binance's statement. The remaining funds are still being traced, which complicates recovery efforts. Binance said it revoked the affected address authorization and engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners. An updated proof of reserves is planned following remediation. User funds are safe, Binance asserted, though that claim remains unverified pending a full technical post-mortem and updated proof of reserves. User funds are safe, the company stated, and any losses will be covered through its Secure Asset Fund for Users and company reserves. That claim is a company assertion, not an independently verified finding. A completed technical post-mortem and updated proof of reserves have not yet been published. Independent verification of customer-fund status remains pending. The reported entry point raises broader questions about whether large exchanges adequately separate deployment access from financial authorization. The alleged breach path points to a structural question about privilege management at large exchanges. Deployment access and financial authorization are different functions, and the incident raises questions about whether controls separating those functions were sufficient. Binance has not yet published a full technical post-mortem. Until it does, the complete picture of how this happened remains incomplete.

Binance said “user funds are safe,” but did not immediately provide proof of this claim. The company said it will “publish an updated proof of reserves once the remediation is complete.”

Spokesperson Andie Cooper said in a statement shared with TechCrunch on Friday that some $3 billion has been frozen by industry partners. The spokesperson said Binance has “begun recovering affected assets for users and continues to work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace, freeze and recover additional funds.”

It’s unclear how the hack went down or under what circumstances the employee’s laptop was compromised, but it’s not uncommon for security incidents to stem from the use of compromised software on employee devices.

Software is generally built from many components, including open source projects, which hackers regularly target , compromise and modify in order to steal data from devices that the affected software is installed on. Other times, malware bundled with regular-looking apps and games can allow hackers to steal usernames, passwords, and session tokens from infected computers, which may let them log in as if they were a legitimate employee.
Binance will face questions about why the company’s security allowed a single employee’s laptop to access systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in funds.

Spokespeople for Binance did not respond to an email with questions about the breach. TechCrunch has also asked the company who, if anyone, performed a security audit of Binance’s network and systems prior to the hack. Companies regularly ask third-party companies to stress-test their security to identify weaknesses that could be exploited by attackers, but it’s unclear if Binance sought such a review.
Security researchers at TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and forensic company, attributed the breach to North Korean hackers, and called it the “largest hack in history.”

Researchers describe the network of hackers, known in the cybersecurity industry as TraderTraitor, as a North Korean cell focused almost exclusively on stealing crypto from large companies and exchanges. This group was also blamed for the now-second-largest heist on record, a $1.4 billion theft from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025 .
According to TRM, the theft of Binance’s billions in crypto took about 20 minutes.

Blockchain security firm Elliptic also attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers. Elliptic said some of the stolen funds ended up in the same wallet that was used in a previous cyberattack on crypto exchange Bitget earlier this year, in which hackers stole $351 million .

The U.S. government and its allies have long warned about the threat from North Korea, which remains cut off from the U.S. and the global financial system for its ongoing development of its nuclear weapons program. Researchers say the breakaway country’s sole motivations are to steal as much crypto as possible in order to continue developing its sanctioned weapons of mass destruction.

CNN reported early Friday that hackers had stolen more than $6 billion from Binance, with several investigators pointing to North Korea and Chainalysis saying it had high confidence in that attribution. The outflows were first spotted on Thursday evening, when about $2.8 billion was reported leaving Binance wallets , and Binance founder Changpeng Zhao later said it looked like a hack . Since then, the picture has changed substantially. In an update on its official X account , Binance moved from “investigating reports” to a confirmed incident: Binance said it is working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the funds, and told users to rely only on its official channels. Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said about $6.36 billion was moved from Binance wallets across 10 blockchains on Thursday, most of it within about 20 minutes starting at 4:05 p.m. US Eastern time, or 20:05 UTC. According to CNBC , TRM said the attack showed preparation well before the theft, including transaction signatures obtained in advance. That fits Binance’s own account: the attacker did not need the wallets’ private keys, because access to the internal withdrawal system was enough to push transfers out. TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group. The FBI named the same group as responsible for the $1.5 billion theft from Bybit in February 2025. Chainalysis chief executive Jonathan Levin also said the firm assessed TraderTraitor as the likely culprit, citing links to earlier attacks. North Korea has previously denied hacking crypto exchanges, Axios noted . The method points in the same direction. Two days before the theft, on October 27, Binance said it had blocked a week of North Korea-linked attacks from a campaign known as Contagious Interview, which uses fake job interviews to trick developers into running malicious code on their machines. Binance has not said whether the compromised engineer’s laptop is connected to that campaign. If the estimates hold, the theft is more than four times the size of the previous record: Ronin Network, March 2022 · about $620M About half of the stolen funds are frozen, mostly stablecoins whose issuers can block their own tokens. The rest is harder to reach. CoinDesk reported that the hacker had split about $1.4 billion in bitcoin across 19 wallets, an asset no issuer can freeze. A Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN that “the cat and mouse game has barely begun,” expecting North Korea to tap money-laundering networks to cash out. Binance says users will not bear the losses, and its next disclosures will be the updated Proof of Reserves and the post-mortem. It's worth noting most modern OLED displays with touchscreens handle touch input this way. As you would expect, you can slide your finger across the screen to scroll through content, and pinch with two fingers to zoom in on photos, documents and web pages. Additionally, it's possible to draw directly on the screen with a finger, allowing you to doodle and annotate notes. Apple suggests professionals will find the touchscreen useful for interacting with 3D objects and getting a feel for how their iOS apps will work, while for everyday users will appreciate it in apps like Pages and Keynote. Borrowing a page from the iPad, you can use your finger to hide the dock . Likewise when you use touch to interact with menus, there's more spacing between items to make it easier to select a specific one. None of the above is groundbreaking, but it never hurts to have multiple ways to interact with a device. The new MacBook Pro sees Apple finally embracing an idea it has spent nearly two decades calling misguided. Steve Jobs famously hated even the thought of adding a touchscreen to the MacBook, going so far as to say using one would be "ergonomically terrible." His successor, former CEO Tim Cook, joked creating a laptop with tablet-like features would be akin to making a fridge with a built-in toaster. Now it will be a question of whether people will want to spend at least $2,899 for the privilege of owning a touchscreen Mac before Apple trickles the feature down to its more affordable computers.

extraction.body: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop. The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well. Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop… The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display. It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays. John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X: We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro. Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399. Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon . Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations. Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration. The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology. While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac. MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself. Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability: Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call. In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage. Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content. I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point? If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful. I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use. The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity. While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.

The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.
Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content.

I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point?

If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful.

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use.

The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.

Well, it’s finally happened: Apple has got with the times and finally made a laptop with a touchscreen . However, while the new MacBook Pros with PROLED screens look like fantastic devices, I think Apple has made a mistake by putting its first laptop touchscreen on the more expensive MacBook Pro, rather than the more mainstream MacBook Air… or even the MacBook Neo . The 14-inch MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starts at $2,899 / £2,899 / AU$4,599, and the 16-inch model starts at $3,399 / £3,399 / AU$5,499. That’s a big ask for most people, especially these days. Of course, MacBook Pros, as the name suggests, are aimed at professionals, and thanks to their high-end components, they should really be seen as investments that allow you to speed up your workflow. Interestingly the new touchscreen MacBook Pros come with Apple’s M5 Pro and M5 Max chips . If you want Apple’s latest M6 chip , you’ll need to go for the non-touchscreen 14-inch MacBook Pro that was announced a few days earlier . Perhaps confusingly, the M6 is less powerful than the M5 Pro and M5 Max, and so far there are no hints that Apple is preparing to release M6 Pro and M6 Max chips. My point is that by putting its first-ever laptop touchscreen on its most powerful — and expensive — MacBooks, Apple is severely limiting the potential audience for the technology. Had it instead put a touchscreen on the more affordable MacBook Air, it could have had a real hit on its hands. As someone who has used plenty of Windows laptops and Chromebooks with touchscreens in the past, I know how useful they can be for certain tasks, and I often miss them when using a MacBook. Being able to scroll down a website with a finger, turn a page in an ebook, or quickly tap a menu item feels natural and intuitive, and I’m sure it will on the new MacBooks. My daughter, who grew up with touchscreens on everything, would also instinctively poke an often sticky, grubby (kids, you’ve got to love them!) finger at a MacBook screen and be surprised when nothing happened. If you’re dropping $3,000+ on a touchscreen laptop just to use the touchscreen for browsing websites, then you’re either super-rich or you should get help with your budgeting. These are all pretty simple tasks and gestures. What I've never used touchscreens on laptops for, however, is for complex tasks and tools, such as recording and editing music in Ableton Live, or editing videos in Adobe Premiere Pro. Instead, for things that needed precision or complexity, nothing beat the good old combo of keyboard and touchpad (or even better, keyboard and a mouse), as well as other external peripherals such as MIDI controllers and drawing tablets . Which leads me to wonder why Apple picked the MacBook Pro, a device that’s supposedly designed for exactly those type of tasks, to showcase its first laptop touchscreen. If you’re dropping $3,000+ on a touchscreen laptop to mostly just to use the touchscreen for browsing websites, then you’re either super-rich or you should get help with your budgeting. The 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and no touchscreen starts at $2,999 / £2,999 / AU$4,799. Of course, MacBook Pros, as the name suggests, are aimed at professionals, and thanks to their high-end components, they should really be seen as investments that allow you to speed up your workflow.

If you want Apple’s latest M6 chip , you’ll need to go for the non-touchscreen 14-inch MacBook Pro that was announced a few days earlier . How would Apple prove that touchscreens on laptops aren’t “ergonomically terrible”? Apple took its time, but it really figured it out”? And it’s just a touchscreen. Apple waited it all out, realized no one cared that much, added a touchscreen with some minor UI improvements, and went, “Okay, enjoy macOS with some swiping.” [Image: This demo from a pro photographer used bracketed exposures and a vibe coded app to composite the images into one interactive photo. coreStoryFacts.text: A new touchscreen Mac requires new software, and with the announcement of the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , Apple detailed just how you'll use your fingers to navigate macOS.
Apple claims this reduces latency, making it "feel like you're touching the content itself." It's worth noting most modern OLED displays with touchscreens handle touch input this way.

Steve Jobs famously hated even the thought of adding a touchscreen to the MacBook, going so far as to say using one would be "ergonomically terrible." His successor, former CEO Tim Cook, joked creating a laptop with tablet-like features would be akin to making a fridge with a built-in toaster.
Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.
While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years.
Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content.
Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined.

Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place.
And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:
The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices.
You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design.
The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support.
We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6.
The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser .
Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.

A new touchscreen Mac requires new software, and with the announcement of the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , Apple detailed just how you'll use your fingers to navigate macOS. The new laptop has an integrated touch sensor built directly into the display. Apple claims this reduces latency, making it "feel like you're touching the content itself." It's worth noting most modern OLED displays with touchscreens handle touch input this way. As you would expect, you can slide your finger across the screen to scroll through content, and pinch with two fingers to zoom in on photos, documents and web pages. Additionally, it's possible to draw directly on the screen with a finger, allowing you to doodle and annotate notes. Apple suggests professionals will find the touchscreen useful for interacting with 3D objects and getting a feel for how their iOS apps will work, while for everyday users will appreciate it in apps like Pages and Keynote. Borrowing a page from the iPad, you can use your finger to hide the dock . Likewise when you use touch to interact with menus, there's more spacing between items to make it easier to select a specific one. None of the above is groundbreaking, but it never hurts to have multiple ways to interact with a device. The new MacBook Pro sees Apple finally embracing an idea it has spent nearly two decades calling misguided. Steve Jobs famously hated even the thought of adding a touchscreen to the MacBook, going so far as to say using one would be "ergonomically terrible." His successor, former CEO Tim Cook, joked creating a laptop with tablet-like features would be akin to making a fridge with a built-in toaster. Now it will be a question of whether people will want to spend at least $2,899 for the privilege of owning a touchscreen Mac before Apple trickles the feature down to its more affordable computers.

The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well. Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop… The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display. It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays. John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X: We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro. Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399. Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon . Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations. Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration. The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology. While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac. MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself. Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability: Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call. In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch. The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI. Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage. Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content. I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point? If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful. I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use. The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models. passages: Apple has officially announced the all-new MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR display , its first touchscreen laptop.

The new machine was first hinted at by Apple on October 19 with the company’s “Pro and tell” experience teaser . Earlier today, new Apple CEO John Ternus shared a “spotlight” teaser for the laptop as well.
Read on for all the details about the new high-end laptop…
The new machine features a light-up Apple logo, tandem OLED, and touch input on the display.
It runs on the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, like the existing MacBook Pro models without OLED touch displays.
John Ternus, who is rocking a new profile picture with the new Mac, shared the first look at the new machine on X:
We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL
Apple previously used a glowing Apple logo on its notebook hardware for years until the 12-inch MacBook and 2016 MacBook Pro.
Pricing for the new laptop starts at $2899 for the 14-inch model. The 16-inch version starts at $3399.
Pre-orders are available starting today with deliveries starting November 6. You can find the product page for the new MacBook Pro here . The new machines are also available on Amazon .
Colors include silver or space black options with standard or nano-texture display configurations.

Beyond the new high-end laptop, Apple also announced the redesigned iPad mini , M6 iMac , and M6 14-inch MacBook Pro this week. Back in March, Apple upgraded the standard 14- and 16-inch MacBook Pro laptops to the current M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
Apple calls the new design both thinner and lighter than the standard MacBook Pro models in the same size configuration.
The new MacBook Pros look awesome with glowing Apple logos. We’re so back. pic.twitter.com/Ce6G8EIVQF
The new MacBook Pro is the first to use what Apple calls a PROLED XDR display, replacing Mini-LED as the MacBook Pro display technology.

While Apple has innovated with multi-touch on the iPhone and iPad, the Mac has been resistant to touch input for years. The new MacBook Pro changes that with the first touchscreen Mac display. Here’s what Apple says about touch on the Mac.

MacBook Pro features Touch for the first time, bringing pros a whole new way to interact with their content. Crafted specifically for the Mac, every touch interaction feels incredibly responsive and refined. Everyday tasks are simple and intuitive, allowing users to scroll through a webpage with a natural swipe; pinch to zoom in on a photo; drag and drop slides from one presentation to another; and double-tap a window to fill the screen, or flick to tile it into place. And the touch sensor is built directly into the display panel — not layered on top of it — reducing latency so users feel like they’re touching the content itself.
Apple also touts the use of a new hinge technology in the MacBook Pro, in part to support touch input without compromising on stability:

Touch also introduces entirely new ways of working for pro users. Graphic designers can now use the entire display as their canvas, no longer constrained by the area of the trackpad when drawing; musicians can play software instruments right onscreen; and app developers can test how Touch performs in their iOS and iPadOS apps directly on the MacBook Pro display. And these new ways to interact with MacBook Pro work in tandem with the keyboard shortcuts and trackpad gestures pros know and love. In addition, a newly designed hinge provides greater stability while using Touch, and advanced video stabilization automatically smooths the camera feed in real time while using Touch on a video call.
In addition to touch as an additional input method, the new MacBook Pro also adopts the Dynamic Island in favor of the notch.
The Dynamic Island now comes to Mac, serving as the home for Spotlight, Live Activities, and Siri AI.

Not interested in touch? The existing MacBook Pro configurations from March stick around at the same prices. You just lose OLED, the glowing Apple logo, and the thinner and lighter design. Performance, however, is pretty much on par between versions as both offer M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.
The new laptops can be configured with up to 128GB of unified memory and 16TB of solid state drive storage.
Peak display brightness jumps from 1600 nits to 2000 nits for HDR content.

I honestly think this is a downgrade. Remember when Apple introduced the Touch Bar? It was supposed to be a big deal, but eventually Apple removed it. Now they’re adding a touchscreen to the MacBook. What’s the actual point?

If it supported the Apple Pencil, I could understand the appeal, especially for designers. But without it, I honestly don’t see much use for it. Maybe I’m wrong, but I’ve used touchscreen Windows laptops before, and I never really found it useful.

I can’t help wondering whether Steve Jobs would have approved of this direction. Apple needs a better marketing team that understands what people actually want, rather than adding a touchscreen that, in my opinion, offers very little practical use.

The 14-inch model is half a pound lighter at just 3 pounds even compared to 3.5 pounds for the same version of the previous design. The overall footprint is reduced as well with 0.59 x 12.24 x 8.52 inch dimensions compared to 0.61 x 12.31 x 8.71 inch dimensions when comparing 14-inch models.

The 16-inch model is notably lighter as well. The new design weighs in at 4 pounds even compared to 4.7 pounds for the previous design. Dimensions change to 0.63 x 14 x 9.62 inches compared to 0.66 x 14.01 x 9.77 inches between designs.
Playing piano on the touchscreen MacBook Pro pic.twitter.com/lDlwIeqErd

The new machines still use Touch ID with no Face ID support. Apple also doesn’t offer built-in cellular models of the new MacBook Pro. We’ll have to keep waiting for Face ID and built-in cellular connectivity.
You can find Apple’s press release for the new machines here . All configurations are available to order from Amazon .

sources.title: Oops! Apple just put its first laptop touchscreen on the wrong MacBook - TechRadar
passages: In an ideal world, then, Apple would have put its touchscreen on an entirely new 2-in-1 MacBook, but I can’t see that happening any time soon.
Apple sort of has a device like that — the powerful iPad Pro , which can be paired with a Magic Keyboard that turns it into a touchscreen laptop.
The problem there, however, is that despite coming with Apple’s powerful M-series chips, the same you’ll find in MacBooks, the iPad Pro is limited to the iPadOS operating system and mobile apps.

However, while the new MacBook Pros with PROLED screens look like fantastic devices, I think Apple has made a mistake by putting its first laptop touchscreen on the more expensive MacBook Pro, rather than the more mainstream MacBook Air… or even the MacBook Neo .

Instead, for things that needed precision or complexity, nothing beat the good old combo of keyboard and touchpad (or even better, keyboard and a mouse), as well as other external peripherals such as MIDI controllers and drawing tablets .

A touchscreen MacBook Neo for $899, say, could be a real hit, especially if Apple was to also keep the non-touchscreen model for people who still want the ultimate affordable way to get into the Mac ecosystem.
This isn’t just an Apple problem, of course.
I’ve spent a decent amount of time with each one at various events, and I found that the touchscreen was the least-used part of the laptop — in fact, I often forgot those laptops had one.
Because there aren’t cheaper, non-touch, models, though I didn’t resent its inclusion.
Until then, I’ll stick with my standard MacBook Pro, and just try to remember not to prod it with my sausage fingers too often.
Perhaps confusingly, the M6 is less powerful than the M5 Pro and M5 Max, and so far there are no hints that Apple is preparing to release M6 Pro and M6 Max chips.

My daughter, who grew up with touchscreens on everything, would also instinctively poke an often sticky, grubby (kids, you’ve got to love them!) finger at a MacBook screen and be surprised when nothing happened.
