extraction.body: SINGAPORE/PARIS/BOSTON: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time. Cryptocurrency prices fell ​on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets. The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion. “We NEVER use any customer funds, so they are not impacted,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said ‌in a post on ‌X. Teng described the breach as a “complex attack” that was not carried out by one person and ​included ‌a ⁠compromised laptop ​as well ⁠as malicious software designed to delete traces and evidence of its activity as it went along, “making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate.” The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, Internet-connected wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. The bulk of the Binance heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs ⁠and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a ‌2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea. “TRM attributes the attack ‌to ... North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis on its website. Both TRM ​and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. “This incident ‌is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind,” British blockchain analysts Elliptic said. North Korea has for years used state-linked cyber units for ‌espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to US and South Korean authorities as well as cybersecurity experts. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment. Binance is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Secret Service (USSS), a person familiar with the situation told Reuters. The FBI said it was “aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate ‌investigative steps.” The USSS did not respond to an emailed request for comment. Abu Dhabi’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance’s main operating license, said it was “engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident.” “It’s the biggest ⁠hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market ⁠maker GSR said, as crypto prices fell broadly. Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3 percent to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilized.

passages: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said $6.3 billion of funds are involved in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest-ever hack.
Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion of tokens.
For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback.
The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency.
“The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said in a post on X.
“We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.”
“The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data.

“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”

An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange.
The company said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.”
The hackers appear to have exploited how Binance authorizes transactions, according to TRM.
Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said North Korea was behind the heist, which it called “the largest crypto theft on record.”

extraction.body: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said $6.3 billion of funds are involved in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest-ever hack. Digital tokens fell. “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said in a post on X. “We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.” Binance has temporarily suspended all withdrawals, which it expects to resume within 48 hours, co-founder Yi He said in a post on X. The company said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.” Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said North Korea was behind the heist, which it called “the largest crypto theft on record.” “TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” the firm said. “We make this judgment with high confidence.” Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion of tokens. For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback. Notorious previous episodes of theft and fraud among fallen crypto giants such as FTX and Mt. Gox set the stage for protracted bear markets, bruises the industry has worked to put behind it in US President Donald Trump’s promised new era of regulatory clarity for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin dropped 3% at the end of the US session and a further 3% in Asia trading, falling below $77,000 to its lowest level since September, with other tokens also selling off. “The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data. “Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.” The hackers appear to have exploited how Binance authorizes transactions, according to TRM. They seemingly gained access to the exchange’s systems and used internal software to authorize transfers across 10 different blockchains, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, it said. Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop. “We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak,” the company said. An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around $1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024. The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than $1.5 billion of the stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group Inc., said $800 million of its coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.” Sentiment was already fragile after a spate of crypto security incidents. In recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget, while tampering tied to Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses. “Attackers are operating at unprecedented speed and scale” but “the tools to track and trace operate at that speed too,” said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs. “Stablecoin issuers freeze within hours. Investigators follow funds across chains in real time.” Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with $11 billion in options set to expire Friday. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry. Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt. Gox eventually went bankrupt. “It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.” The Binance incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. More than 700 Polymarket users were drained of $2.7 million in funds, said blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps, in a post on X. A spokesman declined to comment on the numbers. Recent security incidents haven’t been confined to crypto firms. South Korea’s Daishin Securities disclosed a data leak affecting about 38,000 customers this week, and Mirae Asset Global Investments reported a hacking incident, Yonhap reported. In Japan, hackers on Tuesday threatened to release data of traders using a GMO Internet Group cloud service for foreign-exchange trading. — Bloomberg

sources.title: World’s biggest crypto heist: Hackers steal US$6.3 billion from Binance
passages: SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.
TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S.
Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.

Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.

World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
“Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
“Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang. North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. ‘Biggest hack in history’ North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts. Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. “Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8 per cent, while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy MSTR.O fell nearly 6 per cent in extended U.S. trading. Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. “Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. “It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong. Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report. The crypto exchange runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a $1 billion reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that “and company funds” will cover losses. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

sources.title: Binance targeted in $6.3 billion crypto heist, the largest ever
passages: The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.
The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025.
Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange.

The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X.
About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said.

Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges.
Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change.

The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence.

The company has suspended all deposits and withdrawals while it works with law enforcement to secure its infrastructure and locate stolen funds. The hack originated from a compromised laptop, it said, which allowed “an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.” “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said late Thursday on X. About $3 billion of crypto assets that transited through wallets connected to the hackers have so far been identified and frozen, the company said. Binance will “cover all losses” from the hack, it said, adding, “User funds are safe.” “We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice,” it said. Binance is the world’s largest cryptocurrency trading platform by volume, with hundreds of thousands of users who buy, sell and store billions of dollars’ worth of digital currencies on the exchange. Unlike traditional bank deposits, funds kept in accounts with companies like Binance are not automatically insured against losses, potentially leaving any refunds up to the discretion of individual exchanges. The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025. Binance cautioned that the full value of assets affected by the hack, as well as assets recovered or frozen, could change. “This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” it said. Bitcoin was down about 4.3%, while Ethereum lost 4.6% of its value. Two major stablecoin issuers, Tether and Circle, said they had identified billions of dollars in assets connected to the hackers and had frozen them. Tether froze more than $1.567 billion worth of its digital currency, CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X. Jeremy Allaire, CEO of stablecoin issuer Circle, said the company had also frozen hundreds of millions of dollars of assets and was coordinating with law enforcement. The massive breach of Binance occurs at a moment when cybersecurity defenses around the world are on high alert about the possibility of novel attacks facilitated by recent advances in artificial intelligence. In 2025, Coinbase disclosed that thieves had stolen customers’ personal information and tried to extort the company for $20 million. Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao, said, “As a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.” Zhao stepped down as the CEO of Binance in 2023 and pleaded guilty to breaking U.S. anti-money-laundering laws.

coreStoryFacts.text: Hackers siphoned off $6.3 billion from crypto exchange Binance in the biggest heist that the digital-asset industry has ever faced, the latest in a slew of security incidents afflicting the financial sector.
Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said $6.3 billion of funds are involved in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest-ever hack.
Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion of tokens.
For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback.
The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency.
“The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said in a post on X.
“We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.”
“The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data.

“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”

An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange.
The company said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.”
The hackers appear to have exploited how Binance authorizes transactions, according to TRM.
Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said North Korea was behind the heist, which it called “the largest crypto theft on record.”

SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.
TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S.
Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.

Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.

World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
“Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
“Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

extraction.body: Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, said $6.3 billion of funds are involved in what the industry is describing as crypto’s biggest-ever hack. Digital tokens fell. “The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B,” Binance said in a post on X. “We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.” Binance has temporarily suspended all withdrawals, which it expects to resume within 48 hours, co-founder Yi He said in a post on X. The company said it will cover all losses and “user funds are safe.” Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs said North Korea was behind the heist, which it called “the largest crypto theft on record.” “TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” the firm said. “We make this judgment with high confidence.” Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion of tokens. For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident is a potential setback. Notorious previous episodes of theft and fraud among fallen crypto giants such as FTX and Mt. Gox set the stage for protracted bear markets, bruises the industry has worked to put behind it in US President Donald Trump’s promised new era of regulatory clarity for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin dropped 3% at the end of the US session and a further 3% in Asia trading, falling below $77,000 to its lowest level since September, with other tokens also selling off. “The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data. “Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.” The hackers appear to have exploited how Binance authorizes transactions, according to TRM. They seemingly gained access to the exchange’s systems and used internal software to authorize transfers across 10 different blockchains, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, it said. Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop. “We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak,” the company said. An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around $1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024. The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than $1.5 billion of the stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group Inc., said $800 million of its coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.” Sentiment was already fragile after a spate of crypto security incidents. In recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget, while tampering tied to Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses. “Attackers are operating at unprecedented speed and scale” but “the tools to track and trace operate at that speed too,” said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs. “Stablecoin issuers freeze within hours. Investigators follow funds across chains in real time.” Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with $11 billion in options set to expire Friday. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry. Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt. Gox eventually went bankrupt. “It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.” The Binance incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. More than 700 Polymarket users were drained of $2.7 million in funds, said blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps, in a post on X. A spokesman declined to comment on the numbers. Recent security incidents haven’t been confined to crypto firms. South Korea’s Daishin Securities disclosed a data leak affecting about 38,000 customers this week, and Mirae Asset Global Investments reported a hacking incident, Yonhap reported. In Japan, hackers on Tuesday threatened to release data of traders using a GMO Internet Group cloud service for foreign-exchange trading. — Bloomberg

passages: SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.
TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S.

BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.

Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.

World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.

Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
“Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses.
“Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.

Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.

extraction.body: SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang. North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. ‘Biggest hack in history’ North Korea has ​for years ⁠used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well ⁠as cybersecurity ​experts. Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. “Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8 per cent, while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy MSTR.O fell nearly 6 per cent in extended U.S. trading. Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. “Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. “It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong. Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report. The crypto exchange runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a $1 billion reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that “and company funds” will cover losses. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

passages: The digital currency exchange Binance says it was the target of a $6.3 billion crypto heist Thursday, believed to be the largest ever recorded.
The previous record for a crypto heist was $1.5 billion that hackers from North Korea stole from Bybit in February 2025.

Reform UK did not answer further questions about whether the party was continuing its relationship with the third-party contractor, and whether any action was taken against them. The 32-year-old was arrested in 2022 after a woman was raped while she slept in a caravan at the Royal Windsor horse show. Dinnage was later charged over the attack in 2025. But just months before his conviction, he was hired as security for Mr Farage as the Reform UK leader hit the campaign trail in April and May for the local elections. Dinnage was seen accompanying Mr Farage across parts of the UK, including Waterlooville in Hampshire, Worthing in West Sussex, and Downham Market in Norfolk. Reform UK admitted that Dinnage acted as Mr Farage’s security after being hired via a third-party contractor. The party has insisted the contractor told them an extensive security vetting process had been carried out before he was hired. “As soon as we found out, we were shocked and disgusted and he ceased to be used by Reform,” a spokesperson told The Guardian. But questions are being asked about Reform’s security vetting process and how the party allowed a man facing a rape charge to hold a position of responsibility near members of the public and a high-profile politician. A Labour spokesperson said: "Nigel Farage must urgently explain at what point Reform UK became aware that they allowed a man charged with rape to directly interact with the public on their behalf. They must also urgently make clear what action they have taken to prevent such a situation happening again. “Farage and his party are lurching from scandal to scandal and the public are rapidly seeing who they really are. In recent weeks Farage has shrugged off vile misogyny and Reform has an appalling track record when it comes to standing up for women. It’s time Farage showed some leadership for once, got his house in order, and realised the buck stops with him.” Mr Farage has long been vocal about the need for MPs to be served with greater protection amid heightened threats. The matter was brought to the public eye once over the summer week following the murder of veteran politician Ann Widdecombe. extraction.body: Ryan Dinnage – who accompanied Reform UK leader on walkabouts before local elections – was later jailed, raising questions about vetting failure One of Nigel Farage’s security team who accompanied him on the local election campaign trail this year was facing a rape charge and was later jailed for eight years, raising questions about a failure of vetting. Ryan Dinnage spent time protecting Farage in April and May, but in June was convicted of having raped a woman while she slept in a caravan at the Royal Windsor horse show. Dinnage was seen beside Farage on walkabouts on at least four occasions on Reform’s local election campaign trail this spring: in Llandudno, Conwy County; Waterlooville, Hampshire, Worthing, West Sussex, and Downham Market, Norfolk. He had been charged in 2025, three years after the crime took place at the equestrian event in 2022. Reform UK acknowledged Farage was provided with protection by Dinnage, and said his services had been supplied by a third-party contractor who had assured them he had been vetted. A spokesperson for the party said: “As soon as we found out, we were shocked and disgusted and he ceased to be used by Reform.” However, the episode raises questions about how a security operative facing a charge of serious sexual violence could have been put in a position of responsibility near a senior politician and members of the public. Reform UK did not answer further questions about whether the party was continuing its relationship with the third-party contractor, and whether any action was taken against them. A Labour spokesperson said: “Nigel Farage must urgently explain at what point Reform UK became aware that they allowed a man charged with rape to directly interact with the public on their behalf. They must also urgently make clear what action they have taken to prevent such a situation happening again. “Farage and his party are lurching from scandal to scandal and the public are rapidly seeing who they really are. In recent weeks Farage has shrugged off vile misogyny and Reform has an appalling track record when it comes to standing up for women. It’s time Farage showed some leadership for once, got his house in order, and realised the buck stops with him.” Farage is generally accompanied by a large security team, and has spoken of threats being made against him. The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe has been charged with engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism, including against Farage. Over the summer, counter-terror police reopened a year-long investigation into an alleged firebomb attack at Farage’s home in south London. The Reform UK leader has repeatedly said he accepted a £5m gift from the crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne in order to pay for his security for the rest of his life. He has previously turned down taxpayer-funded security from the government, which included a bodyguard, a car, and a trained driver, deeming it to be inadequate. Dinnage, then 32, of Croydon, was sentenced to eight and half years in prison in July. According to Thames Valley police, his offence took place in the early hours of 16 May 2022, when Dinnage entered the caravan where the victim was sleeping and raped her. He was reported to police later that day and arrested the next day. Reform is not the only party in the spotlight for a vetting failure in recent weeks. The Conservatives were criticised, by Reform UK, for having employed a former election candidate, Jack Ross , who was filmed by an undercover reporter appearing to discuss the cost of hiring contract killers. Ross had worked as a consultant in Kemi Badenoch’s office. Ross is facing an investigation by the Tories after he was filmed apparently asking an undercover reporter: “What do you want done?” and apparently offering to “broker” the services of an alleged far-right paramilitary group. Police in Scotland have said they will be reviewing an Al Jazeera documentary in which Ross was filmed seemingly making a range of comments about what a contract killer could be employed to do, and talked about using far-right groups to create disruption on the streets. But questions are being asked about Reform’s security vetting process and how the party allowed a man facing a rape charge to hold a position of responsibility near members of the public and a high-profile politician. It’s time Farage showed some leadership for once, got his house in order, and realised the buck stops with him.” Mr Farage has long been vocal about the need for MPs to be served with greater protection amid heightened threats. extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September . Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . extraction.body: After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro , which it later went on to remove . The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display. In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound. The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors. Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant. The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399. Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6. The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September . Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction . The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999 . It’s been a long road for Apple to get here When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works . After watching Apple's iPhone Duo launch I was struck by one detail — its support for the Apple Pencil , which makes it the first iPhone to support the device. When Steve Jobs launched the iPhone in 2007 he famously posed the rhetorical question “Who wants a stylus?”. His argument was that you already have the best stylus you’d ever need with you at all times — your fingers. Touchscreen displays have gone on to dominate smartphone and tablet design, and have proved far superior to the stylus as a way of navigating a software interface; but the humble stylus has always had its advocates, and it has never really gone away. Some Samsung devices in particular can be used with a stylus — the S Pen . And, of course, Apple eventually capitulated and introduced the Apple Pencil for the iPad Pro, turning the tablet into a digital drawing pad for illustrators, artists and anyone who simply likes to sketch out ideas. Perhaps I should clarify that Apple 's first successful stylus was the Apple Pencil (2nd edition), rather than the original Apple Pencil. The original Apple Pencil had a terrible design that meant you had to remove a tiny, easily lost cap to charge it, and worse, the Pencil’s Lightning connector plugged directly into the iPad. That left the Pencil sticking precariously out of the tablet, so it was easy to knock, and seemingly designed to snap either the connector or the iPad’s port at some point. It also had no built-in way to attach securely to the iPad for storage. In terms of Apple’s design failures, the original Apple Pencil is right up there with the Apple Magic Mouse, which has the charging port placement underneath, so it can’t be charged and used at the same time. Amazingly, that’s still the current design of the Magic Mouse, but Apple quickly did something about the Apple Pencil. The Apple Pencil was fixed with the second-generation, which was released alongside a redesigned iPad Pro in 2018. Instead of plugging directly into the iPad’s Lightning port (such a bad idea) it attached magnetically to the iPad’s side, where it effortlessly paired, charged wirelessly and stayed stored. That eliminated both the precarious protruding connector and the removable cap. So would Steve Jobs really be turning in his grave right now to know that Apple’s new phone works with its stylus? I’m not so sure. I went back and watched ​​the original iPhone keynote from 2007 . Talking about styluses Jobs said, “Yuck! Who wants a stylus? You have to get ‘em, put ‘em away and you lose them. Nobody wants a stylus! [...] We’re going to use the best pointing device in the world. We’re going to use a pointing device that we’re all born with. We’re born with ten of them, we’re going to use our fingers. We’re going to touch this with our fingers.” Looking back, we can forgive him some of the hyperbole about the stylus at the launch of the iPhone because he was introducing what, for many people watching, was previously unthinkable — a way of using a screen-based smartphone that relied on just your fingers, and he had a battle to win people over and a point to make. In the broadest sense, he was right — touchscreen displays have proved far superior to the stylus as a way of navigating an interface; but the stylus has never really gone away. Of course, back in Apple’s history there was another device that had a stylus, the Apple Newton MessagePad . It launched in 1993, came with a plastic stylus for writing, tapping and using its much-mocked handwriting recognition software. Jobs killed off the Newton in 1998, shortly after his return to Apple. Apple generally called the Newton’s stylus a pen, rather than giving it a standalone product name. So the Apple Pencil wasn’t Apple’s first stylus. It was the company’s return to pen input after Steve Jobs had famously ridiculed styluses when introducing the iPhone. The Apple Pencil was introduced four years after Jobs’ death in 2015, but I think he would have approved. People genuinely seem to love the Apple Pencil, despite it still having some flaws (there’s no eraser on the other end, for example) and it could even be the secret weapon in Apple’s new iPhone Duo’s success. The fact that you can use the Apple Pencil with the new iPhone Duo immediately locks Apple’s new foldable phone tightly into Apple's ecosystem of connected devices. The Apple Pencil is expensive, but a lot of iPhone Duo buyers will already own an Apple Pencil, because Apple households tend to have quite a number of Apple devices already in them. (It would be wise to check which version of the Apple Pencil you own though, since the Apple press release only says the "iPhone Duo will support Apple Pencil with USB-C). And that’s what could make Apple Pencil support much more than another feature on the spec sheet. The iPhone Duo’s folding screen gives people a larger canvas, but the Pencil gives them a reason to use it — for drawing, handwriting, annotating documents and editing photos with precision. Jobs’s real objection was to a stylus you needed simply to operate a phone; on the iPhone Duo, your fingers would still handle that perfectly well, and the Pencil would step in when it was genuinely the better tool. It’s been a long road for Apple to get here
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .
After watching Apple's iPhone Duo launch I was struck by one detail — its support for the Apple Pencil , which makes it the first iPhone to support the device.

When Steve Jobs launched the iPhone in 2007 he famously posed the rhetorical question “Who wants a stylus?”. His argument was that you already have the best stylus you’d ever need with you at all times — your fingers.

Touchscreen displays have gone on to dominate smartphone and tablet design, and have proved far superior to the stylus as a way of navigating a software interface; but the humble stylus has always had its advocates, and it has never really gone away.

Some Samsung devices in particular can be used with a stylus — the S Pen . And, of course, Apple eventually capitulated and introduced the Apple Pencil for the iPad Pro, turning the tablet into a digital drawing pad for illustrators, artists and anyone who simply likes to sketch out ideas.

Perhaps I should clarify that Apple 's first successful stylus was the Apple Pencil (2nd edition), rather than the original Apple Pencil. The original Apple Pencil had a terrible design that meant you had to remove a tiny, easily lost cap to charge it, and worse, the Pencil’s Lightning connector plugged directly into the iPad. That left the Pencil sticking precariously out of the tablet, so it was easy to knock, and seemingly designed to snap either the connector or the iPad’s port at some point. It also had no built-in way to attach securely to the iPad for storage.

In terms of Apple’s design failures, the original Apple Pencil is right up there with the Apple Magic Mouse, which has the charging port placement underneath, so it can’t be charged and used at the same time. Amazingly, that’s still the current design of the Magic Mouse, but Apple quickly did something about the Apple Pencil.

The Apple Pencil was fixed with the second-generation, which was released alongside a redesigned iPad Pro in 2018. Instead of plugging directly into the iPad’s Lightning port (such a bad idea) it attached magnetically to the iPad’s side, where it effortlessly paired, charged wirelessly and stayed stored. That eliminated both the precarious protruding connector and the removable cap.
So would Steve Jobs really be turning in his grave right now to know that Apple’s new phone works with its stylus? I’m not so sure.

I went back and watched ​​the original iPhone keynote from 2007 . Talking about styluses Jobs said, “Yuck! Who wants a stylus? You have to get ‘em, put ‘em away and you lose them. Nobody wants a stylus! [...] We’re going to use the best pointing device in the world. We’re going to use a pointing device that we’re all born with. We’re born with ten of them, we’re going to use our fingers. We’re going to touch this with our fingers.”

Looking back, we can forgive him some of the hyperbole about the stylus at the launch of the iPhone because he was introducing what, for many people watching, was previously unthinkable — a way of using a screen-based smartphone that relied on just your fingers, and he had a battle to win people over and a point to make. In the broadest sense, he was right — touchscreen displays have proved far superior to the stylus as a way of navigating an interface; but the stylus has never really gone away.

Of course, back in Apple’s history there was another device that had a stylus, the Apple Newton MessagePad . It launched in 1993, came with a plastic stylus for writing, tapping and using its much-mocked handwriting recognition software. Jobs killed off the Newton in 1998, shortly after his return to Apple.

Apple generally called the Newton’s stylus a pen, rather than giving it a standalone product name. So the Apple Pencil wasn’t Apple’s first stylus. It was the company’s return to pen input after Steve Jobs had famously ridiculed styluses when introducing the iPhone.

The Apple Pencil was introduced four years after Jobs’ death in 2015, but I think he would have approved. People genuinely seem to love the Apple Pencil, despite it still having some flaws (there’s no eraser on the other end, for example) and it could even be the secret weapon in Apple’s new iPhone Duo’s success.

The fact that you can use the Apple Pencil with the new iPhone Duo immediately locks Apple’s new foldable phone tightly into Apple's ecosystem of connected devices. The Apple Pencil is expensive, but a lot of iPhone Duo buyers will already own an Apple Pencil, because Apple households tend to have quite a number of Apple devices already in them. (It would be wise to check which version of the Apple Pencil you own though, since the Apple press release only says the "iPhone Duo will support Apple Pencil with USB-C).

And that’s what could make Apple Pencil support much more than another feature on the spec sheet. The iPhone Duo’s folding screen gives people a larger canvas, but the Pencil gives them a reason to use it — for drawing, handwriting, annotating documents and editing photos with precision. Jobs’s real objection was to a stylus you needed simply to operate a phone; on the iPhone Duo, your fingers would still handle that perfectly well, and the Pencil would step in when it was genuinely the better tool. Far from turning in his grave, I suspect Jobs might have appreciated the distinction.

sources.title: The Apple Pencil turned the Duo into my new favorite notebook
passages: The iPhone Duo is not a notebook — although it is the first iPhone to support the Apple Pencil.
I was only, like, 60 percent serious when I set out to turn the Duo into a notebook, but I actually liked the idea the more I got into it.
Even so, I can see the new notebook effect in the eyes of the people I talk to about the Duo.
The Pencil has one other neat trick — it can stick to the Duo’s hinge magnetically when the phone is closed.

extraction.body: Apple’s $2,000 folding phone is a surprisingly good stand-in for a $20 notebook. Believe me; nothing gets me going quite like a new notebook. With this one special new notebook, I will see the world differently. And a few weeks, a month, or maybe a year later, I’ll concede that it didn’t change everything and add it to my notebook graveyard. The iPhone Duo is not a notebook — although it is the first iPhone to support the Apple Pencil. Even so, I can see the new notebook effect in the eyes of the people I talk to about the Duo. “Is that the new iPhone?” the conversation starts. And with this week’s iOS 27.2 update officially adding that Apple Pencil support, it can also be a notebook. That’s the USB-C Apple Pencil, to be specific, so there’s no pressure sensitivity. You do still get the ability to “scribble” handwriting that’s automatically turned into text in apps like Messages or Safari, as you can on the iPad. I asked for some Pencil-friendly app suggestions and downloaded a handful. But having the stylus in my hand led me on an unexpected side quest: turning the whole phone into a notebook. Maybe I could cajole the Duo into being something less distracting, more input-friendly. But I don’t think I curated my way out of the new-notebook trap, even if it was a fun exercise. Notes, unsurprisingly, is where the Pencil is at its best. When you use the Pencil for handwriting in the app, you can enable the auto-refine handwriting feature that neatens up your writing while still keeping its unique characteristics intact. It occasionally gets tripped up by some of my scrawl that it either doesn’t know what to do with or misinterprets — it kept insisting on turning a “u” into an “o” in one instance. And it works after a small delay when you pause your writing, which I can see being distracting if I really want to get into a flow state. The Notes app also has a big homescreen widget that kind of turned the phone into a notebook, but wasn’t nice to look at. When you launch the app, it turns the cover screen into the front of your notebook. You can’t add tags or links between notes, and you’re limited to one notebook. Using the Apple Pencil with the Duo gave me one more reason to love the matte finish on the inner screen. There’s just a bit of resistance moving the pencil across the display that feels more satisfying than the lifeless plastic-on-glass effect of writing on the cover screen. The Pencil has one other neat trick — it can stick to the Duo’s hinge magnetically when the phone is closed. The pencil is longer than the phone, so it’s an awkward fit, but it’s been a handy way to carry both around the house as I relocate throughout the day. I was only, like, 60 percent serious when I set out to turn the Duo into a notebook, but I actually liked the idea the more I got into it. Above all, the new-notebook effect proved to be just as strong as always. The shiny new thing eventually fades into the background. You can — and I will continue to — just carry a little notebook around with your regular phone.

It boasts a 6-core CPU consisting of 2 super-cores at the computer level and 4 energy-efficient cores for AI purposes and easier tasks. Extremely interesting is the 7-core GPU, which is 40% faster between generations and Apple It promises, for example, significantly better handling of AAA games. Of course, the Neural Engine has also been improved for AI tasks, which should run even faster (for example, "retouching" photos and the like).

It is clear that you have given Apple with operating system for iPhone Duo really work. It is clear that it is fundamentally based on iOS, however, it does not lack the multitasking features of iPadOS in the form of natural, seamless multitasking. What is very interesting is that Apple he also thought about such details as the glass animation when opening or closing the device, which looks really impressive. But in general, I'm not afraid to say that when opened, it looks iPhone Duo in terms of home screen as classic iPad mini.

But in general, it can be said about multitasking that you cannot expect the same functions from it as from iPads – Apple It primarily showed the world a two-app mode, where each takes up half of the display. So don't expect floating windows of one app above the other. What you can expect, on the other hand, is a half-open device mode, where you can simply open the phone and place it, for example, like a classic desk calendar or, conversely, a notebook. In both cases, iOS It adapts to the device's orientation and displays the content as it should.
Quite interesting are the solutions and animations for live activities, which have so far been tied to Dynamic IslandBut that is no longer the case.

It should also be extremely impressive that iPhone Duo There should be practically no visible fold in the middle, i.e. at the hinge point. All this while maintaining maxthe highest possible display quality combined with durability.

As for the sound, iPhone Duo offers according to the words Apple surround sound in both height and width, and overall it should be a real experience to watch any video on it. But that's not surprising at all, because the aspect ratio of the device is perfect for watching videos.

Also worth noting is the fully hidden front camera under the display on the inside, which creates an unobstructed interior. So that everything works as well as possible in terms of imaging capabilities, Apple added for iPhone Duo to the A20 chip Pro and a special Dual-Display Engine, which ensures perfect functionality.

Other interesting features include the deployment of the C2 5G modem, which should be 50% faster than the C1X. The battery life will also please, which is of course all-day and what's more, this model can be charged to a whopping 50% in 20 minutes.

Although it was generally assumed that the camera of the first flexible iPhone will be the biggest weakness, Apple tried to convince us otherwise at the presentation and I have to say that he was quite successful. The rear camera consists of a 48MPx Fusion wide-angle camera and a 48MPx Fusion ultraThe wide-angle camera seems to be doing really well. As for the aforementioned under-display selfie camera, its quality seems to be very decent. I personally like that FaceTime video calls can be mirrored on both the front and rear displays, so you can actually make calls from both sides.

This function can also be used when taking photos, when the person being photographed can see on the external display what the photographer has in the viewfinder on the large internal display. If you are taking photos of children, you will appreciate that you can play fairy tale animations led by Snoopy on the external display to keep the children entertained during the photo shoot.

extraction.body: Unlock and manage exclusive Techradar member rewards. Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards. It’s been a long road for Apple to get here When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works . After watching Apple's iPhone Duo launch I was struck by one detail — its support for the Apple Pencil , which makes it the first iPhone to support the device. When Steve Jobs launched the iPhone in 2007 he famously posed the rhetorical question “Who wants a stylus?”. His argument was that you already have the best stylus you’d ever need with you at all times — your fingers. Touchscreen displays have gone on to dominate smartphone and tablet design, and have proved far superior to the stylus as a way of navigating a software interface; but the humble stylus has always had its advocates, and it has never really gone away. Some Samsung devices in particular can be used with a stylus — the S Pen . And, of course, Apple eventually capitulated and introduced the Apple Pencil for the iPad Pro, turning the tablet into a digital drawing pad for illustrators, artists and anyone who simply likes to sketch out ideas. Perhaps I should clarify that Apple 's first successful stylus was the Apple Pencil (2nd edition), rather than the original Apple Pencil. The original Apple Pencil had a terrible design that meant you had to remove a tiny, easily lost cap to charge it, and worse, the Pencil’s Lightning connector plugged directly into the iPad. That left the Pencil sticking precariously out of the tablet, so it was easy to knock, and seemingly designed to snap either the connector or the iPad’s port at some point. It also had no built-in way to attach securely to the iPad for storage. In terms of Apple’s design failures, the original Apple Pencil is right up there with the Apple Magic Mouse, which has the charging port placement underneath, so it can’t be charged and used at the same time. Amazingly, that’s still the current design of the Magic Mouse, but Apple quickly did something about the Apple Pencil. The Apple Pencil was fixed with the second-generation, which was released alongside a redesigned iPad Pro in 2018. Instead of plugging directly into the iPad’s Lightning port (such a bad idea) it attached magnetically to the iPad’s side, where it effortlessly paired, charged wirelessly and stayed stored. That eliminated both the precarious protruding connector and the removable cap. So would Steve Jobs really be turning in his grave right now to know that Apple’s new phone works with its stylus? I’m not so sure. I went back and watched ​​the original iPhone keynote from 2007 . Talking about styluses Jobs said, “Yuck! Who wants a stylus? You have to get ‘em, put ‘em away and you lose them. Nobody wants a stylus! [...] We’re going to use the best pointing device in the world. We’re going to use a pointing device that we’re all born with. We’re born with ten of them, we’re going to use our fingers. We’re going to touch this with our fingers.” Looking back, we can forgive him some of the hyperbole about the stylus at the launch of the iPhone because he was introducing what, for many people watching, was previously unthinkable — a way of using a screen-based smartphone that relied on just your fingers, and he had a battle to win people over and a point to make. In the broadest sense, he was right — touchscreen displays have proved far superior to the stylus as a way of navigating an interface; but the stylus has never really gone away. Of course, back in Apple’s history there was another device that had a stylus, the Apple Newton MessagePad . It launched in 1993, came with a plastic stylus for writing, tapping and using its much-mocked handwriting recognition software. Jobs killed off the Newton in 1998, shortly after his return to Apple. Apple generally called the Newton’s stylus a pen, rather than giving it a standalone product name. So the Apple Pencil wasn’t Apple’s first stylus. It was the company’s return to pen input after Steve Jobs had famously ridiculed styluses when introducing the iPhone. It also had no built-in way to attach securely to the iPad for storage.

passages: The iPhone Duo is not a notebook — although it is the first iPhone to support the Apple Pencil.
I was only, like, 60 percent serious when I set out to turn the Duo into a notebook, but I actually liked the idea the more I got into it.
Even so, I can see the new notebook effect in the eyes of the people I talk to about the Duo.

extraction.body: Apple’s $2,000 folding phone is a surprisingly good stand-in for a $20 notebook. Believe me; nothing gets me going quite like a new notebook. With this one special new notebook, I will see the world differently. And a few weeks, a month, or maybe a year later, I’ll concede that it didn’t change everything and add it to my notebook graveyard. The iPhone Duo is not a notebook — although it is the first iPhone to support the Apple Pencil. Even so, I can see the new notebook effect in the eyes of the people I talk to about the Duo. “Is that the new iPhone?” the conversation starts. And with this week’s iOS 27.2 update officially adding that Apple Pencil support, it can also be a notebook. That’s the USB-C Apple Pencil, to be specific, so there’s no pressure sensitivity. You do still get the ability to “scribble” handwriting that’s automatically turned into text in apps like Messages or Safari, as you can on the iPad. I asked for some Pencil-friendly app suggestions and downloaded a handful. But having the stylus in my hand led me on an unexpected side quest: turning the whole phone into a notebook. Maybe I could cajole the Duo into being something less distracting, more input-friendly. But I don’t think I curated my way out of the new-notebook trap, even if it was a fun exercise. Notes, unsurprisingly, is where the Pencil is at its best. When you use the Pencil for handwriting in the app, you can enable the auto-refine handwriting feature that neatens up your writing while still keeping its unique characteristics intact. It occasionally gets tripped up by some of my scrawl that it either doesn’t know what to do with or misinterprets — it kept insisting on turning a “u” into an “o” in one instance. And it works after a small delay when you pause your writing, which I can see being distracting if I really want to get into a flow state. The Notes app also has a big homescreen widget that kind of turned the phone into a notebook, but wasn’t nice to look at. When you launch the app, it turns the cover screen into the front of your notebook. You can’t add tags or links between notes, and you’re limited to one notebook. Using the Apple Pencil with the Duo gave me one more reason to love the matte finish on the inner screen. There’s just a bit of resistance moving the pencil across the display that feels more satisfying than the lifeless plastic-on-glass effect of writing on the cover screen. The Pencil has one other neat trick — it can stick to the Duo’s hinge magnetically when the phone is closed. The pencil is longer than the phone, so it’s an awkward fit, but it’s been a handy way to carry both around the house as I relocate throughout the day. I was only, like, 60 percent serious when I set out to turn the Duo into a notebook, but I actually liked the idea the more I got into it. Above all, the new-notebook effect proved to be just as strong as always. The shiny new thing eventually fades into the background. You can — and I will continue to — just carry a little notebook around with your regular phone.

passages: North Korean hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance , the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in a lightning-fast theft that an insider has called “the largest bank heist in human history.”

State-sponsored hacking unit TraderTraitor was formed around 2016 and tasked with stealing cryptocurrency, according to the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team, a group of 11 nations including the US that tracks North Korean sanctions violations.
A massive $1.5 billion heist targeting crypto exchange Bybit last year was also pinned on the North Korean cybercrime group, given the code name TraderTraitor by the FBI.
US officials have said cybercrime attacks fund roughly half of North Korea’s missile program.
Musk posted several laughing- and grimacing-face emojis on X, his social-media platform, reacting to the news.
Zhao responded by reminding Musk that Binance holds a stake in his businesses worth more than $1 billion.
Cybercriminals swiped the digital coins out of Binance wallets within a mere 20 minutes starting at 4:30 p.m.
ET Thursday, exploiting the system by hacking into an engineer’s laptop, according to analytics firm TRM Labs and industry insiders.
Binance said Friday it has started to recover some of the stolen assets.
Binance initially said the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop.

In an update Friday, Richard Teng, co-CEO of Binance, said the company’s security team has “uncovered additional points of breach,” suggesting it was a complex attack carried out by more than one person.
Binance maintains a $1 billion bitcoin reserve asset fund for users designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
“We make this judgment with high confidence,” the firm said, noting that “several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists.”
